source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The available Bug 1948678 chronology says the Initialize-only fix did not cover two other GetMessageHeader callers: MIME getMsgHdrForCurrentURL and status feedback. That three-caller list is attributed to the author; selected fixed source independently confirms the protocol fast path, MIME nullable header consumer, and callee key-zero early return, while the status-feedback body was not newly inspected. The first beta verification report is immediately qualified by a later comment saying the patch had not actually reached that beta. Later ESR verification identifies128.8.0esr/build20250228160316 after both patches. These are historical reports, not a performance run here. D238540 explicitly requests a comment about the expensive folder traversal; its landed comment explains the ordering constraint. Existing records 170f4df31bb151330b835b27beb0ae0c536f3bcd3c5e967ab0ab6ddc17f3e609 and 9a83effecfd5a1255345c55195f9ec2c25bfcea22b64c47548de18ecad4688d0 own the mechanism. Main comment22 and related1858157 context remain unavailable, so this is a bounded partial lesson with zero audit credit. Backing out1858157 for ESR was suggested, not established as the chosen outcome; replacement rebased ESR attachments supersede earlier approvals, whose later minus flags mean replacement availability.
title: EML performance verification must identify the patch and build actually present
